sentences.text: Hokkaidornis was a large-bodied plotopterid, a group of ancient seabirds, standing about 1.3 meters tall and reaching 1.7 meters in length.
Its wing bones show unique adaptations, with a flattened radius and an ulna that is the largest known for this group.
The bird's pelvis resembled that of modern anhingas, while its foot bone was quite similar to those of today's penguins.
Kazuhiko Sakurai, Masaichi Kimura, and Takayuki Katoh described the genus and species Hokkaidornis abashiriensis in 2008 based on a semi-complete skeleton lacking the skull.
The first remains were found in the Late Oligocene sediments of the Tokoro Formation near the city of Abashiri on the island of Hokkaido.
Hokkaidornis lived during the Chattian stage, from 27.3 to 23.04 million years ago.
